clue.text: Result of unwise drinking from this Roman vessel?

parts.note: hic is the Latin word for 'this', so a Roman would say it
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A warning about drinking too much from an ancient Roman goblet.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm of the diaphragm is a classic consequence of drinking too much or too fast.

clue.text: I misprinted " brave "

annotationWithheld.why: I misprinted " brave " (8): the anagram is of 'I printed', signalled by the 'mis-' inside 'misprinted', so that one word is both fodder and indicator

clue.text: Breakdown of everyone climbing in the little wood

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the copse holds the climbing word

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A collapse among everybody scrambling about in a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ALL into LLA, which goes inside COPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a breakdown, of health or of a structure.

clue.text: Hit the wood in Devil's Combe, Hindhead

parts.note: to punch is to hit
in the game of bowls the balls are called woods

explanation.surface: Striking a ball in a valley in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Devil's Punch Bowl is a large natural hollow at Hindhead in Surrey. A bowl in lawn bowls is called a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep combe at Hindhead, Surrey, is named the Devil's Punch Bowl.

clue.text: A watercourse includes a spring in this case

indicators.note: one thing includes another by holding it inside, so the spring goes within the watercourse

parts.note: a ditch is a narrow channel carrying water
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A stream that has a spring flowing into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word that goes before 'case': a dispatch case, a flat case for carrying official papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch case or box carries state documents, so the answer names this kind of case.

clue.text: 'ware a car gaudily weaving about on this

definitions.text: 'ware a car gaudily weaving about on this

indicators.note: weaving about describes a swerving, disordered path, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Beware a garishly painted car swerving around on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ware' is the old shout 'beware'. The whole clue is the definition as well: a road where a weaving car is a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A divided road with two lanes each way is where a gaudy car might weave about.

clue.text: Like eggs taken on a shining night in Lincs

definitions.meaning: eggs can be cooked gently in simmering water

definitions.text: taken on a shining night in Lincs
definitions.meaning: the folk song The Lincolnshire Poacher: 'tis my delight on a shining night' to take game illegally

explanation.surface: Eggs collected on a moonlit night in Lincolnshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincs is Lincolnshire, an English county; its traditional song celebrates night-time game stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs cooked in simmering water and game taken illegally share this past participle.

clue.text: Beat a Nazi riot in Africa

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crushing a Nazi uprising somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges A NAZI to ZANIA, placed after TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The East African country formed from Tanganyika and Zanzibar lies in that continent.

clue.text: Had Harold only omitted his upward look! Fortune was so unkind

indicators.note: letters omitted are left out of the name
in a down clue upward means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
luck means fortune

explanation.surface: A rueful exclamation that Harold should never have glanced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upward' turns LO into OL; 'omitted' takes OL out of HAROLD to give HARD, and LUCK follows. 'Fortune was so unkind' is the sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the luck was bad is the same as saying fate or chance treated someone badly.

clue.text: She won the gold but lost the race

definitions.text: She won the gold but lost the race

parts.words: She won the gold but lost the race
parts.note: a Greek myth: the swift huntress stopped to pick up golden apples thrown by her suitor and so lost the footrace and her freedom

explanation.surface: An athlete who took gold yet was beaten in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Won the gold' sounds like a medal, but she literally gathered gold apples that Hippomenes rolled in her path, and lost the race that decided her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical huntress who raced suitors and was beaten after stooping for three golden apples.

clue.text: Flag for an anti-bomb marcher

definitions.meaning: a flag or standard carried in procession
someone who wants to ban the bomb, read as one who bans

explanation.surface: A protest flag carried by a nuclear disarmament marcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: a CND marcher wants to ban the bomb, so is one who bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a large flag or placard; and one who bans things can jokingly be called by the same word.

clue.text: Well-cooked chips are heavenly, of the highest order

indicators.note: food that is well cooked has been thoroughly worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for perfectly fried chips as divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, so the adjective means angelic or heavenly.

clue.text: La belle Dame sans Merci Hath thee in (Keats)

definitions.text: La belle Dame sans Merci Hath thee in (Keats)

parts.words: La belle Dame sans Merci Hath thee in (Keats)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from the last lines Keats gives the pale knights in his ballad: the cruel lady holds the knight in a state of bondage

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats's ballad, with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballad's knights cry 'La Belle Dame sans Merci / Hath thee in' and then the missing word, meaning enslaved; the solver completes the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in bondage or enslavement, as the knight is by the merciless lady.

clue.text: Leaders of Sea Cadets often pressed and given the cat

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Naval cadets are pushed hard and then flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a many-tailed whip once used for naval floggings.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given the cat was to be whipped with the cat-o'-nine-tails, i.e. flogged.

clue.text: Iced meat, a variety that's lost much flesh

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frozen meat of a kind that has shrunk a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted and gaunt from illness or hunger has lost a great deal of weight.

clue.text: Does some work, we hear, with this tool

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the sounds stand in for another spelling

parts.note: someone who adds is doing a sum, arithmetic work

explanation.surface: A craftsman carrying out a job with a particular tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests labour, but here it is sums: someone who adds is doing arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like cutting implement with its blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: It's held up by a mugger briefly — quite a puzzle

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: a mugger is an Indian crocodile, and croc is the short form

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: taken as the letters I, T, S

explanation.surface: A mugger's victim's wallet held up in a puzzling case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ITS to STI, which goes inside A CROC. 'Mugger' is not a robber but the marsh crocodile of India.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle where initial letters of lines spell a word.

clue.text: Such a light in the sky, from these signs?

definitions.text: Such a light in the sky
definitions.meaning: a faint glow seen along the ecliptic before dawn or after dusk
relating to the twelve signs of the astrological belt

explanation.surface: A glow in the heavens, perhaps foretold by the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Zodiacal light is a faint sky glow, and the adjective also means belonging to the astrological signs.

clue.text: This race for wine, or to get unemployment benefit?

definitions.meaning: a ... race, where runners hop in bags
an old name for a dry white Spanish or Canary wine
getting the ... means being dismissed from work, which would lead to the dole

explanation.surface: A quiz about a race, a drink and the dole.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack race, sack (an old fortified white wine) and getting the sack (dismissal) all use the same word.

clue.text: Gilbertian fairy's son, out of Perth possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan fairy's son who hails from Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe the shepherd Strephon is half fairy, son of the fairy Iolanthe; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arcadian shepherd in Iolanthe is a fairy down to the waist, his mother being a fairy.

clue.text: Ancient city whose queen did nothing

definitions.text: Ancient city whose queen did nothing

parts.words: Ancient city whose queen did nothing
parts.note: the North African city's founding queen was Dido, whose name splits as 'did' plus O, a nought

explanation.surface: An ancient city with an idle queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Dido founded the city; her name splits as DID O, and O looks like zero, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenician city on the north African coast, Rome's great rival, founded by Dido.

clue.text: Heir assertive is making a row about one

indicators.note: one word goes about another when it surrounds it

parts.note: clamant means noisy, clamorous
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pushy heir is causing a fuss over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who asserts a right, such as an heir pressing a claim to an inheritance.

clue.text: Transmit from vantage point outside Nova Scotia

indicators.note: the first piece stands outside the second, surrounding it

parts.note: coign of vantage is a favourable position; coign is a corner stone or vantage point
NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: Sending something from a lookout beyond Nova Scotia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coign of vantage' is Shakespeare's phrase for a good viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to send them over to a carrier or recipient.

clue.text: Sunny side up ?

parts.note: not fried eggs but the side of the world where the sun comes up, the east

explanation.surface: A short-order cook's call for fried eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The breakfast phrase is a decoy: the side where the sun comes up is the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The East, where the sun rises, is the old word's meaning.

clue.text: French working girl's wild tiger ate Egyptian god

indicators.note: the tiger eats the god, so the god ends up inside it
wild suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Set or Seth is the Egyptian god of chaos

explanation.surface: A Parisian working girl's savage tiger devoured an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TIGER to GRITE, and 'ate' puts SET inside it. The 's after 'girl' is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grisette was a young French working-class woman, often a shop assistant or seamstress.

clue.text: Old tax return in this was somewhat alarming

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: An old tax return that turned out to be worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses SCOT to TOCS. 'Tax return' looks like a form to file, but the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, so it is literally something that alarms.

clue.text: Tompion on the look-out?

parts.note: Thomas Tompion was a famous English clock and timepiece maker, so a timepiece man; read differently, the phrase is someone keeping guard

explanation.surface: A famous clockmaker keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tompion (1639-1713) was the celebrated English maker of clocks and pocket timepieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard or lookout, and also, punningly, a maker of pocket timepieces like Tompion.

clue.text: Line by Lucian possibly-like Mrs Glasse's

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A line of verse written by the Greek satirist Lucian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LUCIAN to CULINA, and 'by' sets the line beside it. Hannah Glasse wrote a famous 18th-century English cookery book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah Glasse's book was on cookery, so its subject matter belongs to the kitchen.

clue.text: Portia was one come to judgment

definitions.text: Portia was one come to judgment

parts.words: Portia was one come to judgment
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock hails the disguised Portia as a wise biblical judge come to judgment

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's heroine described as a judge arriving in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock cries 'A Daniel come to judgment!' when Portia, disguised as a lawyer, seems to rule for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet famed for wise judgment, after whom Shylock names Portia.
